cards.headline:
Doximity adds UpToDate
to its Ask AI tool
cards.body: Doximity is embedding Wolters Kluwer's UpToDate clinical content directly inside Ask, its AI decision support tool.

blocks.cap: As Doximity ramps up its investment in clinical AI tools, the partnership with Wolters Kluwer positions Ask as the front door to clinical knowledge.

blocks.x: Doximity inked a partnership with Wolters Kluwer Health to embed UpToDate's evidence-based clinical content directly within Doximity Ask, the company’s AI clinical decision support tool.

In the coming weeks, at health systems that use both products, clinicians will see an answer based on UpToDate’s 13,000 clinical topics and best practice guides alongside Doximity Ask’s response, without leaving the Ask workflow.

The company aims to become a leading AI platform for doctors, scaling a clinical AI suite that includes its ambient note-taking tool Scribe and Ask. A year ago, Doximity acquired clinical AI company Pathway.

“Every frontier model has read all the same journals. UpToDate stands alone as a gold standard reference from experienced physicians about what happens when there isn't an RCT,” Doximity CEO Jeff Tangney told Fierce Healthcare.
Doximity’s membership includes more than 85% of all U.S. doctors, and its clinical AI tools, including Ask, have been deployed across more than 165 health systems, according to the company.
Competition in clinical AI is intensifying. Wolters Kluwer has also partnered with Epic and Abridge to integrate UpToDate into their AI-powered CDS tools.
